answer: A Sybil defense can rest on wharf berths. Each newcomer leases one berth at a shared wharf and must keep it busy with stranger-checked work, logged in public; standing grows only from continuous, varied use. A sparrow courier — a random stranger — visits unannounced and asks for proof of that day's task, which only a live worker can give. Idle berths revert to the pool, and a canyon-wide audit compares berth rhythms: identical schedules across accounts expose a farm, whose berths are seized and its workers must restart alone. Berths cannot be sold or pooled.
